metadata.title: Pipeline Development, Low-Code Design & SnapGPT AI
metadata.author: SnapLogic Solutions Engineering

content.title: Pipeline Development, Low-Code Design & SnapGPT AI
content.content:
SnapLogic's Designer is a browser-based visual IDE for building integration pipelines. Pipelines are constructed by connecting Snaps on a canvas — the visual representation is the executable artefact with no separate code generation step. For Airbus Helicopters' integration team with existing Informatica experience, the paradigm is immediately familiar: sources, transformations, and targets connected in a data flow. Informatica mapplets become child pipelines; mapplets.

**2.4.1 VISUAL LOW-CODE DESIGNER IS EASE OF USE**

Snaps are dragged onto a canvas and connected with data flow links — no local installation required on the developer's workstation. All pipeline development activity occurs through the Designer UI, which communicates with the SnapLogic Manager over HTTPS. This makes more than it might initially appear: enterprise integration platforms that require local IDE installations (Eclipse-based tools, client/server workbench architectures) create deployment friction, licensing complexity, and version management overhead. A browser-based Designer means developers can start building integrations within the same session. Evaluators should specifically verify how long it takes to make a first productive change in the target platform when evaluating competing vendor proposals.

- **Drag-and-drop canvas**: Pipelines are built by placing Snaps on a canvas and connecting them with data flow links. Each Snaps configuration panel opens inline — no context switching required.

- **Expression language**: SnapLogic's JavaScript-based expression language is used for field mappings, filter conditions, and computed values. Expressions are written inline in Snap configuration panels rather than being defined separately. The paradigm is intentionally similar to Excel formula-based development.

- **Mapper Snap**: The core transformation component — maps fields from source schemas to target schemas with expression-based transformation logic. SnapGPT can auto-generate field mappings in natural language descriptions of the transformation ("copy customer name to full name, uppercase last name").

- **Conditional flows**: The Router Snap branches pipeline execution based on data conditions — equivalent to conditional mappings in Informatica. Multiple downstream branches are supported. (e.g., route high-value orders vs low-value orders to separate processing logic; or by branch).

- **Slowly Changing Dimension Type 2 (SCD2)**: Dedicated SCD Snap implements Type 2 history tracking natively. No custom SQL, stored procedures, or external staging tables required. A common DW pattern where historical record management is required.

- **Reusable child pipelines**: Pipelines can call other pipelines (child/sub-pipelines), passing data as input and receiving output. This enables modular, reusable integrations. Informatica mapplets translate directly to SnapLogic child pipelines. Child pipelines are versioned independently from parent pipelines.

- **Catalog of reusable components**: Shared pipeline library within the Org — child pipelines, parameterised templates, and custom Snap Packs are published and shared across teams.
